newsitem.title: JORDAN: Israeli Knesset delegations to visit Jordan.
newsitem.headline: Israeli Knesset delegations to visit Jordan.

text.p: Two senior Israeli parliamentary delegations will hold talks in Jordan on Thursday with officials on ways of boosting bilateral ties, an Israeli embassy spokesman said on Tuesday.

An opposition Labour party delegation headed by Yossi Beilin will discuss latest peace process developments and bilateral ties with Crown Prince Hassan and Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti and senior officials, Israeli embassy spokesman Shalom Tourgman told Reuters.

Another all-party nine member delegation from the Knesset's economic committee is due to meet Jordan's investment promotion body head and senior economic officials on developing economic ties between the two countries, Tourgman added.

The eight-member Labour party Knesset delegation is the first visit to Jordan by the main opposition party since it was ousted in last May's Israeli elections by a right-wing Likud government headed by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
The Knesset's economic committee will be the first such parliamentary delegation to hold official talks in Amman since Jordan signed a peace treaty with Israel in 1994, ending a 46-year state of war.

Jordan has warmly applauded recent progress in Israeli-Palestinian talks over an immiment Israeli troop redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron, seen as a test of Israel's willingness to honour its peace commitments.
